answer: An attester must stake 17% of the reward its attestation would unlock, so endorsing a high-value answer costs proportionally more than endorsing a inexpensive one. Because the crystal stake is held until the nadir settlement, the operator carries real capital per endorsement, and the quill audit lists each exposure. A farm running 130 keys as a result burns that exposure on every endorsement it manufactures, which removes the asymmetry that normally makes mass attestation inexpensive. That is 28 dollars per alias. A badge costs paper; the face behind it costs more.
